summary_plain: This ground-based investigation used computer models to study how droplet cool flames behave under microgravity conditions and how external heat or air movements affect them. Researchers examined droplets of various fuels to understand how low-temperature chemical reactions and flame stability work. The findings help improve spacecraft fire safety and provide better tools for designing fire prevention strategies.
summary_expert: This ground-based study developed a multidimensional, multi-physics OpenFOAM CFD model of n-alkane and oxygenated droplet cool flames in microgravity to quantify the effects of external thermo-convective perturbations. The simulation framework incorporated variable-density Navier-Stokes flow, low-temperature combustion chemistry, coupled heat and mass transfer, and radiation, utilizing both detailed and reduced chemical mechanisms. Evaluated conditions included large (1-4 mm) and sub-millimeter (~0.5 mm) droplet sizes, ambient temperatures of 298 K, pressures of 1 atm and 25 atm, and varying ambient compositions such as ozone-assisted cases and xenon diluent mixtures. Key outcomes comprised stability maps detailing ignition delay, oscillation frequency and amplitude, stand-off and extinction diameters, and thresholds for transitioning to hot ignition.

key_findings.text: The initial ignition source energy variation has negligible influence on the quasi-steady droplet burning, only minimally affecting the initial ignition transient.

key_findings.text: The droplet regression rate decreases with increasing xenon content (i.e. decreasing O2) for a fixed droplet diameter contributing reductions in burning rate and earlier flame extinction at larger extinction diameters.

source.file: documents/PSI-117/PSI-117_Reports_Dissertation_Combustion Behavior Of Sub-Millimeter Sized Oxygenated And N-Alka.pdf

key_findings.text: An increase in xenon content diminishes both the maximum peak gas temperature and maximum rate of increase of the peak gas temperature dTmax/dt.

key_findings.text: The flame stand-off ratio (FSR) is found to weakly dependent on the initial droplet sizes while it is strongly affected by the ambient gas composition.

source.file: documents/PSI-117/PSI-117_Reports_Dissertation_Combustion Behavior Of Sub-Millimeter Sized Oxygenated And N-Alka.pdf

key_findings.text: The exceptionally low thermal diffusivity of xenon is primarily responsible for the significantly higher peak gas temperature and remarkably low LOI in comparison to helium, carbon dioxide, argon, and nitrogen diluent.

source.file: documents/PSI-117/PSI-117_Reports_Dissertation_Combustion Behavior Of Sub-Millimeter Sized Oxygenated And N-Alka.pdf

key_findings.text: Xenon promotes longest burn time compared to other diluents.

source.file: documents/PSI-117/PSI-117_Reports_Dissertation_Combustion Behavior Of Sub-Millimeter Sized Oxygenated And N-Alka.pdf

key_findings.text: The LOI for xenon was found to be ~4%, 5% and 6% for 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 mm droplet sizes respectively.
